description:
Motivation: Many customers and internal tenants manually tune batching, KV-prefix caching and quantization profiles to hit unit-economics targets. This is error-prone and brittle across workloads. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (1) a set of conservative autotune defaults for batching and caching that are safe for latency-sensitive and throughput-first workloads; (2) a quantization profile generator with curated presets for common model families and compatibility fallbacks; (3) a small unit-economics (uecon) CLI and exporter used by SRE/product to estimate per-token cost savings from candidate config changes.

What this PR does: Adds an autotune controller that samples online request traces (respecting privacy/security flags) and scores candidate batching/cache configs against latency SLOs and cost savings. It ships a default config set (runtime/autotune/defaults.py) intended to be safe as a platform-wide baseline and an experimental mode flag to enable more aggressive tuning per-customer. The quant/profiles module contains presets (fp16, int8, int4 heuristics) and a compatibility map so the controller can select a quantization candidate only when the runtime+model variant supports it. The uecon CLI lets operators run a dry-run cost projection for a workload given a set of candidate changes and export a CSV/JSON report used by pricing/finance.

Design highlights: - Conservative defaults focus on reducing cold-start latencies and avoiding tail-latency regressions by bounding max_batch_latency for chat workloads and enabling prefix/KV caching TTLs aligned with session durations. - Autotune scoring uses a weighted objective: 60% latency SLO compliance, 40% estimated per-token cost reduction; candidates that would violate SLOs are rejected. - Quant profiles prefer zero-precision-drop presets (quant-aware kernels) when available and include graceful fallbacks to fp16 if a quant variant fails. - Rollout is canary-first: suggestions are surfaced via the console preview and then applied to 5% traffic, monitored for 2 hours, then 25% and finally 100% if metrics are green.

Testing & validation: Integration tests emulate mixed chat/text workloads and assert latency SLO compliance across suggestions. Bench perf jobs run a representative QPS sweep to ensure autoscaling/throughput is unaffected. We ran a staged internal rollout on dedicated test clusters and observed median per-token cost reduction of 18-27% for batch-friendly workloads and no measurable latency regressions on chat SLOs.

Operational notes: Autotune is off by default at the tenant level; account-level opt-in enables experimental aggressive mode. All suggestions require either an automated safe-rollout or manual approval depending on customer tier. The uecon exporter includes a confidence score and expected savings range to aid decisions.

Related: ENG-1112 (autotune roadmap), ENG-1130 (unit-econ reporting), SUP-842 (customer request to lower unit cost for high-volume embeddings).
test_plan: Run CI suite (unit, integration, e2e). Kick off perf bench (infra/ci/bench/perf_job.yaml) for canary cluster. Manual canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated monitor (latency SLOs, error-rate, token-cost). Validate uecon reports match observed invoice delta in test account.
expected_savings: 15-40% per-token cost depending on workload (median ~22% observed in internal tests)
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching and caching; quantization profile presets and unit-econ CLI; feature is off by default and requires tenant opt-in for aggressive mode.
review_comments: Maya Singh (2024-05-24): Nice work. Two questions: 1) Can we ensure the autotune controller never increases batch_size for chat sessions with active streaming? 2) Please add an integration test simulating tool-calls and streaming to ensure keyset TTLs don't evict active sessions.

Ethan Morales (2024-05-25): Reply: Good catch on streaming — added a guard to avoid increasing batch_size when streaming is detected (runtime/autotune/defaults.py). Added tests in tests/integration/test_autotune_end_to_end.py to cover tool-calls and streaming sessions.
Luis Ortega (2024-05-26): Left a few nit comments on quant/profiles.py — prefer explicit schema versioning for the presets so the console can render diffs across releases.
Ethan Morales (2024-05-27): Addressed: added a profile_version field and bumped docs. Also added a migration helper for older persisted profiles.
Priya Nair (2024-05-28): CI flaky on first run (kv cache test). Please ensure test is robust and add retry in the integration harness.
Ethan Morales (2024-05-28): Added a deterministic seeding path and retry in test harness; re-ran CI.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass after fix (initial flaky kv-cache test retried)
bench/perf: pass (no regression in throughput for representative workloads)
deployment_steps: Deploy controller and profile generator to canary ring (k8s set image).
Enable console preview for internal teams to review suggestions.
Canary rollout: 5% for 2h monitor -> 25% for 2h -> 100% if green.
Export uecon report and compare to billing for validation after 24h.
If regressions, automatically rollback to previous config and alert SRE oncall.
notes: This change is intentionally conservative as a baseline for platform-wide deployment. Aggressive mode stays tenant opt-in. Follow-up PRs will add more model-family-aware quant profiles and automated A/B costing experiments.
changelog_summary: Autotune defaults for batching/caching; quantization presets; unit-econ CLI and exporter; console preview UI changes; tests and docs.
